MESSAGE:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a name for the delivery van
2. Work out the drop order and timeline meeting all time windows, the break and the 12:00 return  KEY: Only feasible order is B -> A -> C. Leave 08:30, arrive B 08:50, unload to 09:05 (done before 09:30); arrive A 09:30, unload to 09:45 (inside 09:00-10:00); arrive C 10:25, wait until 11:00 (take the 30-min break during this wait); unload 11:00-11:15; back at depot 12:00 exactly (zero slack). A-first fails (B reached 09:40, after opening). Must give order B, A, C with a timeline that respects all constraints.
3. Rewrite the delivery text to be friendlier
4. List three furniture checks before handover
5. Recommend paper vs emailed delivery note
6. Define 'proof of delivery' in a line
7. Draft an evening-before arrival text under 160 characters

ANSWER:
## Tomorrow's route: B → A → C, with no slack on the return

There is only one order that works:

- **B has to go first.** If the driver went to A first, the earliest he could finish there is 09:15, and he'd reach B at 09:40, after it opens.
- **C has to go last.** It can't take anything before 11:00, and A's window closes at 10:00.

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 | Arrive **B** (shop) |
| 08:50–09:05 | Unload at B ✓ done well before 09:30 opening |
| 09:05–09:30 | Drive to A (25 min) |
| 09:30–09:45 | Unload at **A** ✓ inside the 09:00–10:00 window |
| 09:45–10:25 | Drive to C (40 min) |
| 10:25–10:55 | **30-minute break**, parked near C |
| 11:00–11:15 | Unload at **C** ✓ not before 11:00 |
| 11:15–12:00 | Drive back to depot (45 min) |
| **12:00** | **Back at depot** |

**The return has zero slack.** Whatever route he takes, the earliest he can finish at C is 11:15. Adding the 45-minute drive back always gives exactly 12:00, so any hold-up at C or on the way back makes him late. To build in some margin:

- ask C to have someone ready to receive at **11:00 sharp**, and
- agree with whoever set the 12:00 deadline that 12:15 is acceptable if needed.

Earlier in the day there's some room: about 25 minutes at B and 15 at A.

This assumes the drive from C back to the depot takes the same 45 minutes as depot to C.

## Van name ideas

- **Veneer Diesel**
- **The Dovetail**
- **Sir Loads-a-Lot**
- **Hepplewhite** or **Sheraton**, after classic furniture makers

I'd avoid "Chippendale". It's the obvious furniture-maker pick, but some people will think of the male dance troupe, which may be more than you want on a staff vote.

## Friendlier arrival text

> Hi [Name], it's [Driver] from [Business]. I'm on my way with your furniture and should be with you in about [X] minutes. See you soon!

## Three checks before handing over furniture

1. **Condition:** no new scratches, dents or marks. Compare against the condition notes or photos taken at dispatch.
2. **Moving parts:** drawers slide, doors open and close properly, handles and hinges are secure.
3. **Stability:** legs are tight and the piece stands level without rocking.

## Paper or emailed delivery note?

**Emailed**, with the customer's signature captured on a phone or tablet and photos attached. Keep paper notes for customers who ask for them.

## Proof of delivery, for the part-timer

> **Proof of delivery:** a record, usually the customer's signature plus the date, time and photos, showing the item was delivered in good condition to the right person.

## Evening-before text (under 160 characters)

> Hi Sarah, your furniture from Oakwood Restorations is due tomorrow between 9:30 and 10:30. Any problems, call 07700 900123. Thanks!

That's **131 characters** as written. Check the length again once your real business name and phone number are in. For tomorrow's run, the arrival windows would be roughly: **B** 08:45–09:00, **A** 09:30–09:45, **C** 11:00.

**Avoid emojis and curly apostrophes** (’). Many systems then switch to a different character set, which cuts the single-message limit from 160 characters to 70 and can split one text into two or three.
